formation.title: The Empire of Brazil
formation.text:
From the Amazon to the River Plate the land answers to Rio, and no crown of Europe keeps a foothold on the continent. Da Cunha's Emperor of the West has his empire.

What the empire is to be is still open. The constitution of 1824 gave the emperor a moderating power over the whole state: he names the senators for life, dissolves the chamber at will and sends his own presidents to govern the provinces. Ten years later the Additional Act gave the provinces their own legislatures and schools and ended the entailed estates, to keep the federalists inside the empire.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: The Moderating Power
modifiers.text: The emperor names the senators, dissolves the chamber and appoints the presidents of the provinces.

modifiers.name: The Provincial Assemblies
modifiers.text: Each province has its own legislature and its own schools, and the entailed estates are no more.

advances.name: The Navy of Independence
advances.text: On 1 April 1823 Lord Cochrane sailed from Guanabara to blockade Salvador with ships a year old and crews of doubtful loyalty. By August the Portuguese had left Bahia, Sao Luis had fallen and Para had joined the Empire: the war of independence was won at sea.

event.title: The Fleet Comes Home
event.text: The Portuguese squadron sailed out of Salvador on 2 July 1823 with the garrison aboard, and our ships followed it up the coast. Sao Luis fell before the end of the month, and in August Grenfell's brig brought Para over to the Empire. The prizes taken on the way are anchored in the bay, and the crews ask what is theirs.

options.text: Pay the crews their prize money.

modifiers.name: Prize Money Paid
modifiers.text: The crews of the war of independence were paid what they took, and the fleet does not lack for sailors.

options.text: Take the prizes into the navy.

modifiers.name: Prizes in Service
modifiers.text: The Portuguese ships taken in 1823 serve under the imperial flag.

advances.name: The Order of the Southern Cross
advances.text: Pedro I created the Imperial Order of the Southern Cross on the day of his coronation, 1 December 1822. Its honours, and the titles that followed, bound the great families of the provinces to the new throne.

advances.name: The Law Schools
advances.text: The law of 11 August 1827 founded two courses of law, at Sao Paulo and at Olinda, opened in 1828 in the convents of Sao Francisco and Sao Bento. Their graduates became the empire's judges, deputies and ministers.

advances.name: The Coffee of the Paraiba
advances.text: Coffee spread through the Paraiba valley from about 1825, on estates worked by enslaved people. In the 1820s it was a fifth of Brazil's exports; in the 1830s nearly half.

destiny.name: The Emperor of the West
destiny.text: Da Cunha's title has an owner, and the crowns that answer to Rio must be held together: Portugal across the ocean, the provinces of a continent at home. Keep the realm at stability 25 to open the direction chosen at the formation: the moderating power, or the provincial assemblies.

event.title: The Emperor of the West
event.text:
A century ago Luis da Cunha wrote of a king in Rio who would take the title of Emperor of the West. The title is ours now, and with it every crown, province and people that answers to Rio.

An empire is held together or it is not held at all.

options.text: One empire, from the Amazon to the Plate.

destiny.name: The Shores of the Plate
destiny.text: The Banda Oriental cost a war from 1825 to 1828, and the Plate itself was never Brazil's. An Emperor of the West who means his title must hold both banks of the river. Required: own half of the province of the Plate (the Chana lands on the map, from the mouth of the Uruguay to Buenos Aires' shore), and 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: We own half of the province of the Plate

event.title: Both Banks of the Plate
event.text: Our flag flies on both banks of the River Plate. The river that Colonia's merchants and Spain's governors fought over for a century and a half answers to Rio, and the trade of the interior must pass our customs to reach the sea.

destiny.name: Paraguay
destiny.text: In 1750 Portugal traded Colonia for seven of the Jesuit missions of the upper Uruguay, and the Guarani fought the bargain. Asuncion and the land of the missions lie upriver from the Plate, and whoever holds the rivers holds the heart of the continent. Required: own half of Paraguay, and 2,000 gold in the treasury.

event.title: Asuncion
event.text:
Asuncion and the land of the old missions are ours. The Guarani villages along the rivers have seen Jesuits, governors and armies come and go; they will judge us by what we do.

The court must decide how to hold Paraguay: with a garrison on the river, or with the trade that comes down it.

modifiers.name: The Garrison of Asuncion
modifiers.text: Paraguay is held by the fort on the river.

options.text: Open the Parana to our merchants.

modifiers.name: The Parana Trade
modifiers.text: Our merchants work the Parana, and our neighbours watch them warily.

destiny.name: Upper Peru
destiny.text: Colonia's smugglers bought the silver of the Spanish empire across the river from Buenos Aires. An empire that holds the Plate and Paraguay can reach the mines themselves, on the high plain of Upper Peru. Required: own half of the Collao, have silver in one of our markets, and 75 prestige; not before the fifth age.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Silver is produced in the market
Silver is traded in the market

event.title: The Silver of the Collao
event.text: The high plain of Upper Peru is ours, and the silver that once crossed the Plate as contraband now pays the Empire's own treasury. What the crown does with it is the last question of the road west.

options.text: Let the silver buy the trade of the continent.

modifiers.name: The Silver of the Collao
modifiers.text: The silver of Upper Peru buys the trade of the continent.

options.text: Raise an army of the Andes.

modifiers.name: The Army of the Andes
modifiers.text: An army that can march from the Plate to the high plain.

destiny.name: The Para
destiny.text: Para joined the Empire on 15 August 1823, when Grenfell's brig came up the river to Belem. The mouth of the Amazon is the far north of the Empire, and it must be governed as well as held. Required: Belem (Samauma on the map) is ours and has grown into a town, and 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Belem (Samauma) is ours and has grown into a town

event.title: Belem
event.text: Belem has grown into a town worth the name, and the river trade of the Amazon gathers at its quays. The north is part of the Empire in fact as well as in law.

options.text: The mouth of the Amazon is ours.

destiny.name: Olinda and the Courses of Law
destiny.text: In 1828 the course of law of the north opened in the convent of Sao Bento at Olinda, the course of the south at Sao Paulo. The provinces that govern themselves need their own lawyers, judges and deputies. Required: Olinda (Yapuata on the map) is ours and has grown into a city, courses of law stand in two places, and 2,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: Olinda (Yapuata) is ours and has grown into a city
Courses of law stand in two of our locations

event.title: The Graduates of Olinda
event.text:
The first graduates of the courses of law are taking their seats as judges, deputies and presidents of provinces. They are the sons of the provinces' great families, and they have learned to govern.

They can serve the Empire's ministries, or bring order to their own provinces, where their families' power grows with them.

modifiers.name: Graduates in the Ministries
modifiers.text: The graduates of the courses of law staff the Empire's ministries.

options.text: Send them home to keep order.

modifiers.name: Order in the Provinces
modifiers.text: The great families keep order in their provinces, and their power grows with it.

destiny.name: Salvador and the Coffee Trade
destiny.text: In the 1830s coffee became nearly half of what Brazil sold abroad. Salvador, the old capital, and the coffee of the south together make the Empire's wealth. Required: Salvador (Jiribatuba on the map) is ours and has grown into a city, coffee in one of our markets, and 75 prestige.

conditions.text: Salvador (Jiribatuba) is ours and has grown into a city
A market the country is in

children.text: Coffee is produced in the market
Coffee is traded in the market

event.title: The Coffee Empire
event.text: Salvador has grown into a great city again, and the coffee of the valleys fills the holds of ships in every port of the coast. In the 1830s coffee came to nearly half of what Brazil sold abroad.

options.text: Send the coffee to the world by sea.

modifiers.name: Coffee by Sea
modifiers.text: The coffee trade fills the holds of the Empire's ships.

modifiers.name: The Valley Estates
modifiers.text: The estates of the coffee valleys feed and supply themselves.

buildings.name: Course of Law
buildings.text: A course of law in an old convent, where the sons of the provinces learn to be judges and deputies.

buildings.name: Coffee Estate
buildings.text: A coffee estate on the slopes of the valley, its rows of trees worked by enslaved people. Each one cut from the forest adds its harvest to the coffee of the land.

where.text: The location's raw material is Coffee

list.name: The National Guard
list.text: The law of 18 August 1831 abolished the militias and the ordenancas and enrolled every citizen of means in a National Guard, answering to the justices of the peace, the judges, the presidents of the provinces and the minister of justice. Its officers are chosen by councils of the district's leading electors.

list.name: The Justices of the Peace
list.text: Since 1827 each district elects its own justice of the peace, who settles the quarrels of the parish without waiting for a judge named in Rio.

list.name: The Senate of the Empire
list.text: Under the constitution of 1824 the emperor names the senators for life, and convenes and dissolves the elected chamber at his will.

list.name: The Presidents of the Provinces
list.text: Each province is governed by a president named by the crown, who guides the provincial assembly as the emperor guides the chamber.

list.name: The Colonists of Sao Leopoldo
list.text: From 1822 Major Schaeffer recruited families and soldiers in the German lands for the Emperor. Sao Leopoldo was founded on 25 July 1824 at the old royal linen works, with nine families; more than six thousand people followed by 1828, tradesmen among them, beside the battalions of foreign soldiers.
